Process POD5 reads in groups

Source: R/read_pod5.R
process_pod5.Rd

Calls an R function for consecutive groups of reads from a POD5 file or an existing POD5 reader. Each group is read independently, passed to FUN, and then discarded, allowing large files to be processed incrementally without retaining all reads in memory at once.

Usage

process_pod5(
  file,
  FUN,
  part_size = 1000,
  signal = FALSE,
  calibrated = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

file

character A path to a POD5 file or an existing POD5 reader object. Character paths are opened internally and automatically closed when the function exits, including when FUN raises an error. Existing reader objects are used directly and are not closed by this function.

FUN

is the R function to run on each group. Receives one metadata data frame, or one named list when signal is TRUE. Additional arguments are passed through ...

part_size

numeric A positive whole number giving the maximum number of reads processed in each group. The final group may contain fewer reads. Defaults to 1000.

signal

logical whether signal data should be read for each group. If FALSE, only read metadata are obtained. If TRUE, signal vectors are included in the object passed to FUN. Defaults to FALSE.

calibrated

logical whether signal values should be returned as calibrated values rather than raw ADC counts. This argument is only relevant when signal = TRUE. Defaults to FALSE.

verbose

Logical; whether progress messages should be printed at the start and end of processing. Defaults to TRUE.

...

Additional arguments passed to FUN.

Value

Invisibly returns the number of processed reads. Callback results are not retained. Callback errors propagate after closing internally opened files.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
pod5R::process_pod5("reads.pod5", function(reads) {
print(sum(reads$num_samples))
}, part_size = 1000)
} # }
